reconstructed_theorem_text:
Objects: Put d=card(I), c=real(max(d-1,0)) (natural-number subtraction before casting), E=R^I with Euclidean norm, S={x in E: ||x||=1}, V_j(x)=e_j-x_j*x, and L_S f(x)=Laplacian(f)(x)-D^2 f(x)[x,x]-c*Df(x)[x]. Here Df is the Frechet derivative and D^2 f=D(Df). Write R_+=[0,infinity), and let lambda_T be Lebesgue measure on [0,T], transported to R_+ (the given comap of volume restricted to [0,T]). All time integrals below use this measure unless indicated otherwise. A ProgressiveL2Integrand eta on horizon T is a real process eta(t,omega), strongly progressive for the filtration, with (omega,t) -> eta(t,omega) in L^2(P x lambda_T). I_T^j(eta) denotes the supplied completed continuous Ito process driven by the scalar coordinate B_j(t,omega)=(B(t,omega))_j: the pointwise limit of chosen elementary stochastic-integral approximations off their null uniform-Cauchy bad set, zero on that bad set, and held constant after T; at each t<=T it agrees almost everywhere with the L^2-completion integral up to t.

Domains: I is finite with decidable equality; Omega is a measurable space; P is a probability measure; filtration is indexed by R_+; B:R_+ x Omega -> E; X:R_+ x Omega -> S; u:R_+ x S -> E; temperature a:R_+ -> R; f:E -> R; s in R_+.

Quantifiers: Universally: I, its instances, Omega, its measurable structure, filtration, P, B; then the Brownian and usual-conditions hypotheses; X and its measurability/progressiveness/path hypotheses; u and continuity; a and continuity/nonnegativity; the equation hypothesis; f and its smoothness hypothesis; finally s. In the equation: for every T>0, for P-a.e. omega, for every t<=T and every i in I, the equation holds.

Assumptions: The vector Brownian hypothesis means B(0,omega)=0 for every omega; increments on finite families of pairwise disjoint half-open intervals are jointly independent; every continuous real linear functional ell sends B(t)-B(s), s<t, to a centered Gaussian of variance (t-s)||ell||^2; paths are P-almost surely continuous. B is strongly adapted, and for every s<=t the increment B(t)-B(s) is independent of the sigma-algebra filtration(s). The filtration is right continuous, and every P-null subset of Omega belongs to filtration(t) for every t>=0 (completeness at each time). X is jointly measurable and strongly progressive, with P-a.e. continuous paths on all R_+. The function (t,w)->u(t,w) is continuous. a is continuous and nonnegative at every t. f is C^2 at every point of S (ambient ContDiffAt, not merely a restricted derivative). For every positive horizon T, almost surely simultaneously for all t<=T and i: X_i(t)=X_i(0)+integral_0^t [-u_i(v,X(v))-a(v)*c*X_i(v)]dv+sum_j I_T^j(eta_ij)(t), where eta_ij(v,omega)=sqrt(2*a(v))*(delta_ij-X_i(v,omega)*X_j(v,omega)).

Conclusion: For every s>=0, the real function F(t)=integral_Omega f(X(max(t,0),omega))dP has derivative within [0,infinity) at s equal to integral_Omega [-Df(X(s,omega))[u(s,X(s,omega))]+a(s)*L_S f(X(s,omega))]dP.

Scopes: The conclusion is a derivative at every specified s, within the nonnegative real half-line; at s=0 it is a right derivative. The SDE equation has one full-measure event per T, uniform in t<=T and in i. Path continuity has one full-measure event on all R_+. No tangency assumption on u is written.

Constant dependencies: No existential constant or estimate is asserted. d depends only on I; c is the real cast of natural d-1. The noise integrand depends on T for its L^2 packaging, on X,a,i,j, and on the given filtration/measure. The derivative depends on f,u,a and the law of X_s.
